name: archive-peek-remote
description: Peek inside .zip, .7z, .rar, .tar, .gz, .bz2, .xz, .tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz, .jar, .war, .vsix, .nupkg, .apk, .whl, .xpi, .epub, .aar archives without extracting them, in a viewer or as expandable folders in the Explorer. Works with archives on Remote SSH hosts without installing anything on the server.

enumDescriptions: Open archives in the Archive Peek viewer (an editor tab with statistics and a file tree).
Show archives as expandable read-only folders in the Archive Peek section of the Explorer side bar.
archivePeek.openMode.markdownDescription: How archives open when you click them in the Explorer or run **Archive Peek: Open Archive**. The other mode stays available from the context menu (**Open in Archive Peek View** / **Open in Archive Viewer**).

archivePeek.tree.autoDiscover.markdownDescription: List the archives found in the workspace folders in a **Found in Workspace** group of the Archive Peek section. The search runs once (when the section is shown) through VS Code's search service — on a Remote SSH host, the VS Code Server's own search; nothing is installed — and a file watcher keeps the list current. Archives are only listed; each one is read when you expand it.

archivePeek.tree.autoDiscoverFolders.markdownDescription: Folders to search instead of the workspace folders, e.g. `["/tmp/work"]`. Absolute paths are on the host of the workspace (the Remote SSH host in a remote window); relative paths are resolved against each workspace folder. Subfolders are always included. Use this when the workspace is a large folder such as `/`.

archivePeek.tree.autoDiscoverInclude.markdownDescription: Glob pattern of the archives to list, relative to each searched folder (`#archivePeek.tree.autoDiscoverFolders#`, or the workspace folders), e.g. `**/*.tar.gz`. A leading literal path such as `tmp/work/**/*.tar.gz` makes the search start in that folder. If the pattern starts with the searched folder's own path (folder `/opt/app`, pattern `opt/app/**/*.tgz`), that path is not added a second time.

archivePeek.tree.autoDiscoverExclude.markdownDescription: Glob pattern of files and folders not to search. The enabled `#files.exclude#` patterns are always excluded as well.

archivePeek.tree.autoDiscoverMaxResults.markdownDescription: Maximum number of archives listed in **Found in Workspace**.

enumDescriptions: VS Code's search service for local and Remote SSH folders (falls back to listing folders if it doesn't answer within 30 s); listing folders for other file systems such as SFTP providers.
Always VS Code's search service. It never finishes for file systems without a search provider.
Always list folders through the file system provider (workspace.fs.readDirectory). Symbolic links to folders are not followed.
archivePeek.tree.autoDiscoverMethod.markdownDescription: How **Found in Workspace** searches. VS Code can only search local and Remote SSH folders; for other file systems (e.g. third-party SFTP extensions) folders are listed one by one instead.

archivePeek.autoRefresh.description: Automatically refresh opened archives, and any files opened from them, when the archive changes on disk. Remote archives are refreshed when the remote file system delivers change events (Remote SSH does), when the archive editor becomes active again, and when a file is opened from the archive.

archivePeek.remote.maxArchiveSizeMB.markdownDescription: Largest archive (in MB) that is loaded from a remote host (Remote SSH, WSL, containers…). VS Code's file system API can only transfer a remote file as a whole, so the archive is held in memory once while it is copied to the local temp directory. Larger archives show a warning with a **Load Anyway** button.

archivePeek.remote.cacheSizeMB.markdownDescription: Maximum total size (in MB) of local copies of remote archives kept in the OS temp directory. Least recently used copies are deleted first; copies are always deleted when the archive is closed and when VS Code exits.

archivePeek.maxEntries.markdownDescription: Maximum number of entries listed for one archive. Protects against archive bombs with millions of entries.

archivePeek.maxEntrySizeMB.markdownDescription: Largest uncompressed file (in MB) that can be opened from an archive. Protects against decompression bombs.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Browse archives as read-only folders. Right-click an archive in the Explorer and choose **Open in Archive Peek View**, or pick one:
[Open Archive…](command:archivePeek.openInTree)
Or list all archives in the workspace here (only listed; each is read when you expand it):
[Find Archives in Workspace](command:archivePeek.tree.enableAutoDiscover)
Works with local archives and with archives on Remote SSH hosts. [Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22archivePeek%22%5D)
